body: A booted `viola run` wrapper and its fake agent end when the test that booted them ends, on every exit path: pass, fail, timeout, and SIGKILL, which runs no destructor. After a test run no booted wrapper or fake agent is left running.

The shared stamped fixture home is trusted only when its home exists. A stamp marker restored under `target/` whose home is gone (the runner's `/tmp`, reached through the `target/e2e-home` link) leads to a rebuild, not to a verified-home read. A booted wrapper must not refuse with `unverified-cli` for that reason.
New test for the stamp fix: it fails before the fix (marker present, home absent) and passes after it. It is the chunk's first step.

Proof of «killed»: a harness the test owns SIGKILLs a test process mid-run on the fake agent, and a census at its end shows none of that test's own process tree still running. No test sends a kill to a process it does not own.

Re-measure: every place a test boots a wrapper (the shared fixtures and any test that spawns one itself), what ends each one today on each exit path, and what a wrapper loops on once its test is gone, the reason it spun near a full core rather than idled.

If `viola run` itself has to change to end once its PTY or parent is gone (its loop), that change is held to P3's measure. Its exit path still writes no viola bytes of its own to the human's terminal, and its run diagnostics still go only off the terminal.

Any test that waits on a channel or a thread takes a bound under the project's 20 s lint and cannot hang past a failure. Time bounds fall on the test driver, never on a human. A test socket goes under the short `/tmp` root.
The test drives the wrapper's outer side through the existing boundary driver, the outer PTY, and is sequenced on records, not on reading claude's screen content.
No live `claude` starts. A booted test runs on the fake agent only, and live readings gate nothing.
A change to the fake agent's screens puts the `cli_verify` checks in the gate block.

Acceptance of the CI red: the stamped-home hypothesis is tested from the code, not assumed. A green re-run does not close the red. The acceptance evidence is a CI run on an exact cache hit that reads green, with the `test` job's coverage run passing every booted test.

Each directive control names its `--timeout S` and fires with that flag on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases, each filter selecting at least one test. A control id is 16 characters at most. «Holds» means those cases ran and failed with no TIMEOUT line. Each acceptance predicate states the change that would turn it red.
The standing live rig keeps owning only its own processes and is not reworked. Its census is the model for this chunk's census, not a component the chunk changes.

The life of a booted wrapper and its fake agent bound to the test that booted them: on pass, fail, timeout and SIGKILL (which runs no destructor) they end, and after a test run none is left running.

This is the origin of decision/cleanup-ctrl-c-repeated-until-exit and the booted-wrapper shape this chunk must end on every exit path.

body: A booted wrapper does not outlive its test: on every exit path of a test that boots `viola run` (pass, fail, timeout, SIGKILL with no destructor run) the wrapper and its fake agent end; a drop guard alone cannot hold the SIGKILL path.

The stamped home's validity: a stamp marker is trusted only when the home it stamps is present; where the home under the target/e2e-home link (under the runner's /tmp) is absent, the fixture rebuilds it instead of reading a stale marker restored from a CI cache.
A regression test for the stamped home: a stamp marker present with its home absent fails before the fix and passes after it.

The killed proof: a test-owned harness SIGKILLs a test process mid-run on the fake agent and a census of that test's own process tree at its end finds nothing still running, as the standing live rig's census does.
Process hygiene of kills: no test sends a kill to a process it does not own; a kill targets only the test's own process tree, verified by pid and start time before it is sent.
The fake agent's children and process group: how the fake agent and the wrapper's child sit in process groups and how they exit when their parent or PTY is gone, as fixtures may change them.

The wrapper's end once its controlling test is gone: a `viola run` change to end when its PTY or parent is gone is in scope only as P3 measures it; otherwise fixtures and the fake agent only, no product behaviour change.
How a test boots a wrapper: the shared fixtures and any test that spawns a wrapper itself, the harness boot that makes, stamps and starts, and the cleanup that stops agents and removes the home.
Stamps are written only by verify against the fake agent, one verify stamp per build; the rebuild of an absent home goes through that same path, never a hand-written stamp.
Test homes live under target/e2e-home, whose base may be a link to /tmp; the deletion of a home through that link and the checks of the base bind the rebuild.
CI's only cache is rust-cache over target/; the acceptance evidence is a CI run on an exact cache hit that reads green — a green re-run alone does not close the red.

Directive controls: each control names its --timeout S and fires with that flag on an entry filtered to its own cases, a control id within 16 characters; holds means those cases ran and failed with no TIMEOUT line; every acceptance predicate can fail and each filter selects at least one test.
Bounded waits: a test waiting on a channel, a thread or a process exit takes a bound under the project's 20 s lint, root waits bounded below the per-test kill lines, and none can hang past a failure.
A test socket goes under the short /tmp root, in a test endpoint directory made private.
A change to the fake agent's screens puts cli_verify in the gate block; a gate entry naming an installed tool's path is checked against the host before the card.
Child exit is read on the process handle, never on reader EOF, in any test or fixture that waits for a wrapper or fake agent to end.
No live claude start and no mutation run in this chunk; real claude stays local-only and never in CI.
A killed test child is uninstrumented: a test process killed by the proof leaves no coverage profile the coverage run must count.
